title: Polynomial representations of GL(n)
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Branching from GL(n+1) to GL(n) × GL(1): the branching vector and the norm bound
modules.note:
This file treats the branching from `GL(n + 1)` to `GL(n) × GL(1)` for the representations of
`∏ τ, GL (N τ)`. The rows `N τ` are the rows `n τ` together with one new row, given by `ι τ`. A
weight `κ` is given by the numbers `κ τ h` of columns of height `h` at the place `τ`. This file
defines the branching vector and writes products of kernels as the minors of one filling. It
proves the norm bound for an equivariant matrix through the transposed contraction
`New.GL.extendedTensor`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GL.branchVector`: the product of the leading minors to the powers `γ`, with the new row
  first, so that every column of positive height contains it, and to the powers `κ`, with the new
  row last, so that no column contains it.
* `New.GL.weylNormSq_mulVec_le_of_equivariant`: the norm bound for an equivariant matrix whose
  transpose sends the extremal vector to a multiple of the branching vector.

Notions from other files:
* `New.MatrixPoly`: Polynomials over `R` in an array of variables `X (a, i)`, with rows `a : m` and
  columns `i : ℕ`.
* `New.rankAt`: The number of elements of the finite row type n_τ at the place τ;
  `New.GL.rowEquivFin n τ : n τ ≃ Fin (rankAt n τ)` is the fixed numbering of these rows, and a
  row's position is its number.
* `New.permArray`: For maps e_τ from rows to natural numbers, the array over R whose entry at row
  (τ,a), column i is 1 if e_τ(a)=i and 0 otherwise.
* `New.toPoly`: The linear map from coordinate vectors ξ to polynomials, ξ ↦ Σ_i (Gξ)_i b_i, with G
  the Gram matrix `New.weylGram` (`New.weylGramOver` is its image over another ring) and b_i the
  basis `New.nablaBasis` of products of minors; `New.GL.nablaCombination` is ξ ↦ Σ_i ξ_i b_i.
* `New.weylEval`: For an array y, the evaluation vector `ev_y` with entries b_i(y); its polynomial
  under `New.toPoly` is `New.weylKernel n κ y`.

modules.title: Branching from GL(n+1) to GL(n) × GL(1): integral equivariant branching maps
modules.note:
This file constructs the integral branching map from `GL(n + 1)` to `GL(n) × GL(1)` from its
value at one point, proves its norm bound, and shows that it spans the maps that are equivariant
for the unitary block group. Vectors are coordinates indexed by `New.WeylIndexFamily n κ`
(standard fillings), and `New.schur κ z` is the matrix of `z` in these coordinates. `New.weylRep κ
e` is its twist by `det ^ e` on invertible matrices, `New.weylNormSq` is the squared norm for the
Gram matrix, and `New.GL.blockScalar ι g s` is the matrix `diag(g, s)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.SpansBranchingMaps`: a matrix spans the maps that are equivariant for the unitary block
  group.
* `New.GL.exists_int_branching_of_weylKernel`: an integral equivariant matrix from its value at one
  point.
* `New.exists_branching_matrix`: the branching map, its norm bound and its uniqueness.

Notions from other files:
* `New.rankAt`: The number of elements of the finite row type n_τ at the place τ;
  `New.GL.rowEquivFin n τ : n τ ≃ Fin (rankAt n τ)` is the fixed numbering of these rows, and a
  row's position is its number.
* `New.permArray`: For maps e_τ from rows to natural numbers, the array over R whose entry at row
  (τ,a), column i is 1 if e_τ(a)=i and 0 otherwise.
* `New.toPoly`: The linear map from coordinate vectors ξ to polynomials, ξ ↦ Σ_i (Gξ)_i b_i, with G
  the Gram matrix `New.weylGram` (`New.weylGramOver` is its image over another ring) and b_i the
  basis `New.nablaBasis` of products of minors; `New.GL.nablaCombination` is ξ ↦ Σ_i ξ_i b_i.
* `New.weylEval`: For an array y, the evaluation vector `ev_y` with entries b_i(y); its polynomial
  under `New.toPoly` is `New.weylKernel n κ y`.
* `New.GL.branchVector`: the product of the leading minors to the powers `γ` with the new row first
  and to the powers `κ'` with the new row last.
modules.literature:
Branching from GL(n+1) to GL(n) with multiplicity one. Here the branching map is given for one
interlacing pair as an integer matrix that is equivariant over every field of characteristic 0 and
satisfies an explicit norm bound, and every unitarily equivariant map is a multiple of it. That it
is non-zero is not part of the statement. Source: Goodman, Wallach 2009, Theorem 8.1.1;
Zhelobenko, Compact Lie Groups and their Representations, 1973, ch. X; Molev, Gelfand-Tsetlin bases
for classical Lie algebras, arXiv math/0211289.

modules.title: Duality of integral GL(n) representations, mixed weights and the Cartan product
modules.note:
The integral representations of `∏_τ GL(n_τ)` act on lattices with bases of products of minors, and
a weight `κ` counts the columns of each height. For the reversed weight `κ'_τ(h) = κ_τ(|n_τ| - h)`,
the representation of weight `κ` composed with `g ↦ g⁻¹ᵀ` is that of weight `κ'` twisted by a power
of the determinant, through a unimodular, isometric, equivariant integer matrix. With this matrix,
the representation of mixed weight with positive part `kp` and negative part `km` embeds integrally
into the tensor product of the representation of weight `kp` with that of weight `km` composed with
`g ↦ g⁻¹ᵀ`. For a splitting `ε : N ⊕ m ≃ n` of the letters, this embedding sends the Cartan product
of vectors of weights `kp` and `km` to their tensor, and the squared norm of the product is
multiplicative. Finally, the representations of `GL n` with parameters `l` and `-l` are paired
invariantly by an integer matrix.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GL.exists_star_matrix`: the product of the Hodge stars of the columns, a signed bijection
  between basis tensors that replaces each column by its complement.
* `New.GL.exists_int_duality_matrix`: the integer matrix by which the star maps one Weyl module to
  the other.
* `New.GL.IsDualIsometry`, `New.exists_isDualIsometry`: this matrix is unimodular, isometric and
  equivariant; `New.exists_dual_isometry` states these properties as one conjunction.
* `New.GL.MixedCartanEmbedding`: the integer matrix of the embedding and the four properties asked
  of it; `New.GL.weylEvalAt` is the evaluation vector at the array `New.permArray` of a map of rows.
* `New.mixedWeight`: the weight with `kp τ i + km τ (card n - i)` columns of height `i`.
* `New.nonempty_mixedCartanEmbedding`, `New.mixedCartan`: such an embedding exists for this weight,
  and a chosen one.
* `New.Rows.cartanProduct`: the product; `New.Rows.mixedCartan_mulVec_cartanProduct`: `mixedCartan`
  sends it to the tensor of the factors.
* `New.exists_isDualPairing_of_isHCParam`: the pairing is invariant and computes `New.ofAlgForm` at
  `-l`. It is invertible up to the hook number. It is isometric for the Gram norms `New.weylNormSq`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.permArray`: For maps e_τ from rows to natural numbers, the array over R whose entry at row
  (τ,a), column i is 1 if e_τ(a)=i and 0 otherwise.
* `New.nablaFamily`: The module of Borel semi-invariant polynomials of weight `New.diagramWeight`,
  in which `New.nablaBasis` gives coordinates (`New.sum_coords_nablaBasis`).
* `New.weylRep`: The monoid homomorphism from ∏_τ GL(n_τ,R) to square matrices sending g to ∏_τ
  det(g_τ)^{e_τ} times the Schur matrix of g, for integers e_τ.
* `New.schur`: The Schur matrix S_κ(z) of matrices z_τ of size n'_τ×n_τ. Row i holds chosen
  coordinates of b'_i(zy) in the family b_j(y)·∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}. Here b'_i and b_j are the
  standard basis polynomials in the rows n' and n, and d is given by `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.weylEval`: The vector of values of the basis minor products at an array y.
modules.literature:
Known result: Dual of a Weyl module by Jacobi's complementary minors, and the Cartan component. Here
the results are stated for products of GL_n. The duality and the Cartan map are given by integer
matrices that are isometric and equivariant over fields of characteristic 0. The duality has an
integral inverse and the Cartan map has an integral left inverse. Source: Fulton, Harris,
Representation Theory, 1991, section 15.5; Jantzen 2003; for Jacobi's identity, Grinberg, An
Introduction to Algebraic Combinatorics, Thm 6.4.48.

modules.title: Schur modules: semi-invariants, minors, Fock pairing, Schur and Gram matrices
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
This file sets up a polynomial model of the representations of products of general linear groups
over any commutative ring `R`. The variables `X (a, i)` of `New.MatrixPoly m R` form an array with
rows `a : m` and columns `i : ℕ`. A colour map `c` assigns each row a place `τ`, and a weight `κ`
gives the number `κ τ h` of columns of height `h` at `τ`. `New.nabla R c l` consists of the `f` with
`f(y b) = ∏ b(τ, i, i) ^ l(τ, i) · f(y)` for upper triangular `b`, one matrix for each colour, and a
chosen set of products of minors is taken as its basis. The Weyl module is the dual module, written
in the dual basis as `New.WeylIndexFamily n κ → R`; `Lib.GLn.SchurModule.TensorModel` embeds it into
a tensor product of exterior powers. Left substitution `f ↦ f(z y)` and the Fock pairing
`⟨p, q⟩ = p(∂) q (0)` are the main tools. The rows of the Schur matrix expand the substituted basis
elements, so it acts on the Weyl module, and the Gram matrix is the coefficient matrix of the kernel
`New.weylKernel` in the basis.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.jet`, `New.fockPairing`: the pairing `P(∂) F` at `0`, with power series and with polynomials;
  `New.fockPairing_linSubst` computes adjoints of linear substitutions.
* `New.nabla`, `New.nablaFamily`: the semi-invariants under upper triangular matrices acting on
  columns.
* `New.tableauPoly`, `New.IsTableauBasis`, `New.nablaBasis`: products of minors, and a chosen basis
  among them.
* `New.schur`, `New.weylGram`, `New.weylEval`: the matrix of `f ↦ f(z y)`, the Gram matrix and the
  evaluation vectors in that basis.
* `New.mem_nabla`, `New.minor_mem_nabla`, `New.rowSubst_mem_nabla`: membership as an identity over
  all algebras; minors are members; left substitution `f ↦ f(z y)` (`New.rowSubst`) keeps the
  weight.
* `New.fockPairing_comm`, `New.fockPairing_rowSubst`, `New.fockPairing_star_self_pos`: the pairing
  `⟨p, q⟩ = p(∂) q (0)` is symmetric, the adjoint of `New.rowSubst z` is substitution by the
  transposes, and `⟨p̄, p⟩ > 0` for `p ≠ 0`.

modules.title: A basis of minor products for Borel semi-invariants over any ring, by induction on rows
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
Polynomials are in variables `X (a, i)`, where `a` is a row with colour `c a` and `i : ℕ` is a
column (`New.MatrixPoly`). For finitely many rows and `l = New.GL.columnWeight τ h`, the module
`New.nabla R c l` of Borel semi-invariants has a basis of products of minors that does not depend on
the ring `R`. The proof takes leading terms in one row: bordering lifts a family of minor products,
and a leading-term analysis describes the leading term of a semi-invariant.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GL.HasLeadingTerm F γ G`: `F` is `G` times the monomial of exponent `γ` plus smaller terms;
  `New.GL.rowExpansion x` expands in row `x`.
* `New.GL.columnWeight`, `New.GL.ColouredTableau`, `New.GL.minorProduct`: the weight of a family of
  coloured columns, its fillings by rows, and the product of the minors of a filling.
* `New.GL.interlacing l`: the exponents `γ` with `γ i ≤ l i - l (i + 1)` (truncated subtraction).
  For antitone `l`, these are the `γ ≤ l` such that `l - γ` interlaces `l`.
* `New.GL.exists_bordering`: a filling that avoids `x` is lifted to one whose product of minors has,
  in the variables of row `x`, leading term `X ^ γ` times the old product.
* `New.GL.degree_rowExpansion_mem_interlacing`: the leading exponent of a Borel semi-invariant in
  the variables of one row `x` lies in `New.GL.interlacing` of its weight at the colour of `x`.
* `New.GL.HasLeadingTerm.leadingCoeff_mem_nabla`: the leading coefficient of a semi-invariant in row
  `x` is a semi-invariant in the other rows, of the weight lowered by that exponent.
* `New.GL.exists_isStdMinorFamily`: some finite family of fillings has products of minors that are
  linearly independent and span the semi-invariants of its weight over every ring, recorded as
  `New.GL.IsStdMinorFamily`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.nabla`: For a row colouring c and weight l, the module of Borel semi-invariants: polynomials
  f with f(yβ) = ∏β_{τ,ii}^{l(τ,i)} f(y) for generic upper triangular matrices β_τ, one per colour.
* `New.minor`: For an h-tuple I of rows, the polynomial determinant of the h×h matrix of variables
  in rows I and the first h columns.
* `New.GL.alternant`: For x in ℂ^N and l : ℕ → ℕ, the alternant det(x_i^{l(N−1−j)+j}), 0 ≤ i, j < N,
  if l(N) = 0, and zero otherwise.
modules.literature:
Known result: The standard basis theorem for Schur (dual Weyl) modules over any ring, with their
character. Here the module is the space of polynomials on matrices that are semi-invariant under a
triangular group, for several row colours at once. It lies in the span of a set of products of
minors built one row at a time rather than the semistandard tableaux, and this set is linearly
independent over every ring. For a single colour its character is given by Weyl's quotient of
alternants. Source: De Concini, Eisenbud, Procesi, Young diagrams and determinantal varieties,
Invent. Math. 56 (1980); Akin, Buchsbaum, Weyman, Schur functors and Schur complexes, Adv. Math. 44
(1982), II.2.16, II.4.11.

See also `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Character.WeylCharacterFormula`.

modules.title: Schur matrices, the standard basis of ∇, its weights and the highest vector
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
Polynomials are taken in the entries of an array y with rows (τ, a). Here κ_τ(h) is the number of
columns of height h at the place τ; `New.rankAt n τ` = |n_τ|, and
λ = `New.diagramWeight (rankAt n) κ` has λ(τ, k) = Σ_{k<h<|n_τ|} κ_τ(h). The products
b_i = `New.nablaBasis` of minors of y along standard fillings form a basis of the module
∇ = `New.nablaFamily` of Borel semi-invariants. The Schur matrix S_κ(z) = `New.schur κ z` of a
family of matrices z_τ records the expansion of b'_i(zy); for square z this gives a polynomial
representation of ∏_τ GL(n_τ), which `New.weylRep` twists by integer powers of determinants. For one
place and a one-row shape, S_κ over ℂ is a symmetric power, and, over a topological ring, S_κ(z) is
continuous in z for square z.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.linearIndependent_nablaBasis`, `New.range_nablaCombination`: the b_i form a basis of ∇ over
  every commutative ring.
* `New.sum_schur_smul_nablaBasis`, `New.GL.schur_eq_of_expansion`: row i of S_κ(z) is characterised
  by the expansion of b'_i(zy) in the products b_j(y) ∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}, with
  d = `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.schur_map`, `New.schur_mul_left`, `New.schur_mul_right`, `New.schur_apply_eq_prod`: base
  change, multiplicativity, and the product over the places τ.
* `New.schur_diagonal`, `New.weyl_character`: diagonal matrices and Weyl's character formula.
* `New.weylRep κ e` is the matrix representation of `∏ τ, GL (n τ) R` of weight `(κ, e)`: the Schur
  matrix `New.schur κ g` twisted by the powers `det (g τ) ^ e τ`, with integer exponents `e τ`.
* `New.map_nablaBasis_eq_map_weylKernel_mul_weylEval`: fix enumerations e_τ of the rows. Let φ be a
  linear form with φ(b_i) ≠ 0 only if λ(τ, e_τ(a)) ≤ `New.tableauWeight` i τ a for every row (τ, a).
  Then φ(b_i) = φ(k)·b_i(y). Here y is the permutation array of e (`New.permArray`), and k is the
  kernel `New.weylKernel` at y, a substitution (`New.rowSubst`) of the product `New.highestPoly` of
  leading minors, with value k(y) = 1. So on the span of the b_i, φ is determined by its value on k.

Notions from other files:
* `New.schur`: The Schur matrix S_κ(z) of matrices z_τ of size n'_τ×n_τ. Row i holds chosen
  coordinates of b'_i(zy) in the family b_j(y)·∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}. Here b'_i and b_j are the
  standard basis polynomials in the rows n' and n, and d is given by `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.rowSubst`: For matrices z_τ of size n'_τ×n_τ, the algebra homomorphism f ↦ f(zy) sending
  variable y_{(τ,b),i} to Σ_a z_τ(b,a) y_{(τ,a),i}.
* `New.WeylIndexFamily`: The type of families choosing, for each place τ, a filling in the chosen
  standard set with rows n_τ, heights below |n_τ| and multiplicities κ_τ.
* `New.schurDetExp`: The natural number κ_τ(|n_τ|) if |n_τ| < |n'_τ|, and 0 otherwise, as a function
  of the place τ.
* `New.FitsRanks`: For row families n and n', the condition, at every place τ, that |n_τ| ≤ |n'_τ|
  and κ_τ(h) = 0 for |n_τ| < h < |n'_τ|.
* `New.detPow`: The product over places τ of the determinant of the variables in all rows of block τ
  (fixed enumeration) and first |n_τ| columns, raised to e_τ.

modules.title: The Weyl module inside the tensors of its diagram
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
A tensor in the product of exterior powers, one factor for each column of the diagram, is written as
a function on the column fillings `New.ColumnFilling`, which index the basis tensors.

* `New.fillingMatrix`: the integral matrix that embeds the Weyl module into tensors. Its row at a
  column filling holds the coordinates, in the standard basis, of the product of minors
  `New.fillingPoly` of that filling.
* `New.fillingMatrixOver_mul_schur`: the Schur matrix of a family of square matrices, one for each
  place `τ`, is the restriction of their action `New.minorsMatrix` on tensors.
* `New.span_fillingPoly`: the products of minors span the module of Borel semi-invariants, whose
  dual is the Weyl module.
* `New.exists_fillingMatrix_leftInverse`: the Weyl module is a direct summand of the integral
  tensors.
* `New.exists_fillingMatrix_mulVec_eq_iff_mem_span`: the Weyl module over `ℤ` consists of the
  integral tensors in the span over `ℚ` of the tensors of rational matrices.

Notions from other files:
* A `Tableau` lists the entries of each column; `tableauPoly R e T` is the product, over the columns
  of the tableau `T`, of the `minor` whose rows are the images under `e` of the entries. Here
  `minor R I` is the determinant of the variables `y` in the rows `I` and the first columns;
  `MatrixPoly ι R` is the ring of polynomials in these variables `y`, indexed by `ι × ℕ` (a row and
  a column number).
* `nablaBasis R n κ`, the standard basis, is a chosen basis of products of minors of the module
  `nablaFamily R n κ`, indexed by `WeylIndexFamily n κ`; `nablaCombination κ` takes a coordinate
  vector to its combination of this basis. A vector of the Weyl module is given by its coordinates
  `WeylIndexFamily n κ → R` in the dual basis.
* `rowSubst z` substitutes `z y` for `y`, and row `i` of `schur κ z` holds the coordinates of
  `rowSubst z` of the basis element `i`; so `schur κ z` acts on the Weyl module.
modules.literature:
Known result: the Weyl module over `ℤ` as a direct summand as a ℤ-module of a tensor product of
exterior powers. Source: Akin, Buchsbaum and Weyman, Schur functors and Schur complexes.

modules.title: The Weyl kernel and its Gram matrix: the hook number bound, positivity, Schur's lemma
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
This file studies the reproducing kernel `K(x, y) = f(yᵀ x)` (`New.weylKernel`), where
`f = New.highestPoly` is the product of leading principal minors. `G = New.weylGram` is the integer
Gram matrix of `K` in the basis `b_i = New.nablaBasis` (products of minors) of the semi-invariants
`New.nablaFamily`. The hook number `New.hookNumber κ N = ⟨f, f⟩ = f(∂) f(0)` is the Fock pairing
of `f` with itself. It is positive and at most `(L ^ L) ^ 3` when the diagrams have at most `L`
boxes in total (`New.hookNumber_pos`, `New.hookNumber_le`). This file also proves that the unitary
group is Zariski dense, and derives Schur's lemma for the Schur matrices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.toPoly_weylEval`, `New.toPoly_schur`: `New.toPoly`, `ξ ↦ ∑ (G ξ)_i b_i`, sends the vector
  `ev_y = (b_i(y))` (`New.weylEval`) to `K(·, y)`. It turns the Schur matrix of `z` into
  substitution of `zᵀ`, applied after multiplying by the determinant powers `New.detPow` with
  exponents `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.fillingMatrix_transpose_mul_self`: `G` is the matrix of the form restricted from tensors.
  Hence `G` is symmetric, positive definite, and makes the Schur matrices of `g` and `gᵀ` adjoint
  (`New.weylGram_isSymm`, `New.weylGramOver_posDef`, `New.weylGramOver_mul_schur`).
* `New.mem_range_scalar_of_commute_schur`: a matrix that commutes with `New.schur κ g` for all
  unitary `g` is scalar.

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeylIndexFamily n κ`: families that choose, for each place `τ`, a standard filling with rows
  `n τ`; they index the basis `b_i`.
* `New.schur κ z`: the Schur matrix `S_κ(z)` of matrices `z τ` of size `n' τ × n τ`. Row `i`
  holds the coordinates of `b'_i(z y)` in the products `b_j(y) · ∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}`, where `b'` is
  the basis for the rows `n'` and `d = New.schurDetExp n n' κ`.

modules.title: Fock pairing, Hermitian norm and Cartan products for the Gram matrix of the Weyl kernel
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
This file uses the Fock pairing `⟨P, Q⟩ = P(∂) Q (0)` (`New.fockPairing`) and Schur's lemma to show
that the Gram matrix `G = New.weylGram` times the matrix of the Fock pairings of the basis
`b_i = New.nablaBasis` (products of minors) of the semi-invariants `New.nablaFamily` is the hook
number `New.hookNumber κ N = ⟨f, f⟩`, the Fock pairing of `f = New.highestPoly` with itself.
It treats weights with one row at each place. It defines the squared
norm `New.weylNormSq ξ = re (ξ* G ξ)` and builds a tight frame of integral vectors. It shows that
this norm is submultiplicative under Cartan multiplication of polynomials of weights `κ` and `κ'`,
and defines the products of determinants `New.pairedDetProd`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.weylGram_mul_fockPairing`, `New.fockPairing_toPoly_nablaBasis`: by Schur's lemma, `G` times
  the matrix of the Fock pairings `⟨b_i, b_j⟩` is the hook number `New.hookNumber`.
* `New.GL.comulMatrix`: the matrix `C`, in the bases `New.nablaBasis`, of multiplication of
  polynomials of weights `κ` and `κ'` into those of weight `κ + κ'`;
  `New.GL.vecMul_comulMatrix_eq_iff`: acting on row vectors, `C` multiplies polynomials;
  `New.GL.comulMatrix_mulVec_weylEval`: acting on columns, it sends an evaluation vector to a tensor
  product of two.
* `New.GL.comulMatrix_isometry`, `New.GL.comulMatrix_equivariant`, `New.GL.hasLeftInv_comulMatrix`:
  `C` is an isometry for the Gram matrices, intertwines the Schur matrices, and has a left inverse
  over `ℤ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeylIndexFamily n κ`: families that choose, for each place `τ`, a standard filling with rows
  `n τ`; they index the basis `b_i`.
* `New.schur κ z`: the Schur matrix `S_κ(z)` of matrices `z τ` of size `n' τ × n τ`. Row `i`
  holds the coordinates of `b'_i(z y)` in the products `b_j(y) · ∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}`, where `b'` is
  the basis for the rows `n'` and `d = New.schurDetExp n n' κ`.
* `New.mem_range_scalar_of_commute_schur` (`Lib.GLn.SchurModule.WeylKernel`): Schur's lemma, a
  matrix that commutes with `New.schur κ g` for all unitary `g` is scalar.

modules.title: Fillings whose columns begin with the leading rows
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
At each place `τ` the rows `n τ`, in the order `rowEquivFin`, are `q τ` leading rows followed by as
many later rows as `m τ` has. A filling of the later rows, for the diagram without its first `q τ`
rows, becomes a filling of all rows: the leading rows go on top of each column, and a column of
height `h < q τ` gets the first `h` rows. The hook number of the smaller diagram times the product
of minors of this filling is the polynomial of an integral vector of the Weyl module.

* `New.leadingWedge`: puts the first `q τ` rows on top of a filling of the later rows.
* `New.aeval_fillingPoly_leadingWedge`: where the top blocks of `y` are invertible, its product of
  minors at `y` is a factor independent of the filling times the product of minors of the given
  filling at the Schur complement of `y`.
* `New.leadingWedgeMatrix_mulVec_weylEval`: the induced map on tensors sends the tensor of the
  evaluation vector at an integer array `y` to that at `diag(1, y)`.
* `New.exists_fillingMatrix_mulVec_eq_leadingWedgeMatrix_mulVec`: hence it maps the smaller Weyl
  module into the larger one.
* `New.exists_toPoly_eq_hookNumber_smul_leadingWedge`: the integrality statement.

The integrality statement follows from `New.GL.exists_toPoly_eq_hookNumber_smul` for the smaller
diagram, carried over by the map of tensors above, and the formula for the determinant of a block
matrix by the Schur complement (`Matrix.det_fromBlocks₁₁`).

Notions from other files:
* `rankAt n τ` is the number of rows at `τ`, and `rowEquivFin n τ` numbers them by
  `Fin (rankAt n τ)`.
* `ColumnFilling n κ`: for each of the `κ τ h` columns of height `h < rankAt n τ`, an
  `IncreasingMap (rankAt n τ) h`, that is a strictly increasing sequence of `h` row numbers.
* `fillingPoly ℤ T`: the product of the minors that the columns of the filling `T` cut out of the
  array of variables `X (row, column)`, as an element of `MatrixPoly`.
* `WeylIndexFamily n κ` indexes the standard basis of the Weyl module for the column counts `κ`,
  `toPoly n κ` sends a coordinate vector in this basis to its polynomial, `fillingMatrix n κ`
  embeds this module into the tensors, and `hookNumber` is the Fock pairing of the product of
  leading minors with itself.
modules.literature: Part of a known result, the branching rule from GL(n+1) to GL(n), for any number of removed rows.

modules.title: Algebraic representations of GL(n) on unitary groups: Schur orthogonality
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
A weight `(κ, e)` consists of the numbers `κ τ h` of columns of height `h` and an exponent `e τ` of
the determinant. Only the heights below `card n` enter the index type `New.WeylIndex n κ` and, for
square matrices, `New.schur`. `New.weylRep κ e g` is `∏ τ, det (g τ) ^ e τ` times `schur κ g`. These
representations are restricted to products of unitary groups `U(s)^Φ`. The file defines the
hermitian Gram form, which is invariant when all signs are `1` (`New.gramForm_conjWeylRep`, in
`Lib.GLn.SchurModule.SchurNorm`), and the highest vectors.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.conjWeylMatrix`, `New.conjWeylRep`: the conjugate action of weight `(κ, e)`, as matrices and
  as a representation: `g` acts by `New.weylRep κ e` at the entrywise complex conjugate of `g`.
* `New.gramForm`: the hermitian form `ξ* G η` of the Gram matrix `G = weylGramOver`.
* `New.decreasingPosition`, `New.highestVector`: the order that a vector `l` puts on the rows, and
  the evaluation vector at the frame of that order.
* `New.weylRep_coeff_eq_prod_weightMinors`: the matrix coefficient of `New.weylRep κ e` at a highest
  vector is a product of the functions `New.weightMinors`, products of principal minors.
* `New.schur_orthogonality`: Schur's orthogonality relations on the compact group U(n)^Φ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.schur`: The Schur matrix S_κ(z) of matrices z_τ of size n'_τ×n_τ. Row i holds chosen
  coordinates of b'_i(zy) in the family b_j(y)·∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}. Here b'_i and b_j are the
  standard basis polynomials in the rows n' and n, and d is given by `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.WeylIndex`: The type of families of chosen standard fillings over the places, in the case
  where the row type is the same finite type n at every place, that is
  `WeylIndexFamily (fun _ ↦ n) κ`; `WeylIndexFamily` allows a row type n_τ at each place τ.
* `New.nablaBasis`: For a family i of chosen standard fillings, the polynomial b_i, the product over
  the places τ of the minor products of the fillings i_τ.
* `New.weylEval`: For an array y, the vector of the values b_i(y).
* `New.weightMinors`: For a matrix `g` and integer weights `l`, the product over integers `t` of the
  principal minor of `g` on `{i | t ≤ l i}`, each factor with `t ≤ 0` divided by `det g`.

modules.title: Irreducibility under U(n)^Φ, polarisation and averaging of determinant polynomials
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
The representations `New.conjWeylRep κ e` of the compact group U(n)^Φ are irreducible, and so is the
module `New.nablaFamily` of semi-invariant polynomials.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.span_conjWeylRep_eq_top`, `New.mem_span_rowSubst_unitary`: irreducibility under U(n)^Φ, for
  coordinate vectors and for semi-invariant polynomials.
* `New.exists_pairedDetProd_eq_sum_unitary`: for `card p < card n`, a product of determinants
  `det (η τ k * Y τ)` is a combination of unitary translates of one product of powers of minors,
  with coefficients independent of `Y`.
* `New.exists_forall_eq_mul_map_det_pow`: a linear form `M` that takes the unitary translates of a
  polynomial `q` in square matrices to `t * ∏ τ, det (u τ) ^ c τ` has
  `t = a * M (∏ τ, det (z τ) ^ c τ)`, with `a` depending only on `q` and `c`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.conjWeylRep κ e`: the action of U(n)^Φ on the coordinate vectors `WeylIndex n κ → ℂ` by the
  Schur matrices of the conjugate matrices, times the powers `e` of their determinants;
  `USign (1 : n → ℤˣ)` is the unitary group U(n).
* `New.nablaFamily`: the module of Borel semi-invariant polynomials in rows (τ,a), coloured by τ,
  whose weight has `κ τ h` columns of height `h` at τ, for the heights below |n_τ|.
* `New.rowSubst`: for matrices z_τ, the substitution f ↦ f(zy).
* `New.pairedDetProd`: the element ∏_τ ∏_k det(η_{τk} Y_τ) of a ℂ-algebra S, for n×p matrices Y_τ
  over S and complex p×n matrices η_{τk}.
* `New.Rows.variableMinor`: the minor det(x_{τ,i(a),j(b)}) of the matrix of variables at τ, in rows
  i and columns j.
modules.literature:
Irreducibility under U(n) is part of the known theory of the contravariant form on Weyl's lattice.
See `Lib.GLn.SchurModule.SchurNorm`.

modules.title: Norm bound for Schur matrices and basic facts on the weight representations
modules.group: Schur modules and representations of GL(n)
modules.note:
Let `S(z) = New.schur κ z` be the Schur matrix of rectangular complex matrices `z τ` of size
`n' τ × n τ`, assuming `New.FitsRanks n n' κ`. Let `G` and `G'` be the integral Gram matrices
`New.weylGram` for `n` and for `n'`. The file gives a formula for `S(w)ᴴ G' S(z)` and bounds the
norm of `S(z)` for these forms. It then proves base change, integrality and invariance of the Gram
pairing for the matrices `New.weylRep` and the action `New.Space.weightRep` of the rational unitary
group of `New.stdSpace`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GL.schur_conjTranspose_weylGram_schur`: `S(w)ᴴ G' S(z) = ∏ det(wᴴ z) ^ d · G S(wᴴ z)`, with
  `d = New.schurDetExp n n' κ` the number of columns of height `#(n τ)` if `#(n τ) < #(n' τ)`, and
  `0` otherwise.
* `New.weylNormSq_schur_le`: there are numbers `ρ τ i ≥ 0` (in the proof, the squares of the sorted
  singular values). Their sum over `i < #(n τ)` is at most the sum of the squared absolute values of
  the entries of `z τ`. The Schur matrix multiplies the squared norm by at most the product of the
  `ρ τ i`, to the powers given by the weight `New.diagramWeight`.
* `New.stdSpace_weightRep_apply`, `New.map_weightRep`: γ acts by `New.weylRep` at the matrices
  Φ_τ(γ̄), also after a ring map σ out of ℂ. Here Φ_τ is the embedding that the CM type chooses at
  τ.
* `New.gramForm_conjWeylRep`, `New.gramForm_map_weightRep`: the Gram pairing `New.gramForm` is
  invariant under the compact unitary groups, and under rational γ after any ring endomorphism σ of
  ℂ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.schur`: The Schur matrix S_κ(z) of matrices z_τ of size n'_τ×n_τ. Row i holds chosen
  coordinates of b'_i(zy) in the family b_j(y)·∏_τ det(y_τ)^{d_τ}. Here b'_i and b_j are the
  standard basis polynomials in the rows n' and n, and d is given by `New.schurDetExp`.
* `New.conjWeylRep`: The action of ∏_τ U(s) on coordinate vectors of weight κ by `New.weylRep` at
  the complex conjugate matrices; `New.Space.weightRep` is its restriction to rational points.
modules.literature:
Known result: The contravariant form on Weyl's lattice, the Fischer product, and irreducibility
under U(n). This file treats only the contravariant form: its adjoint formula, its invariance under
U(n), and a bound of operator norms by singular values. Source: Jantzen, Representations of
Algebraic Groups, 2nd ed. 2003; Goodman, Wallach, Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants, 2009,
ch. 5; Howe, Perspectives on invariant theory, 1995.
